subject.title: refactor(codex): keyed turn routing, client-scoped rate limits, and resume subscription safety

question: Should maintainers land this broad Codex app-server ownership refactor as the fix for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101338 after conflict resolution and live proof, or split the pieces into smaller PRs?
rationale: The code direction matches the canonical issue and upstream Codex contracts, but the change spans session routing, auth-profile rate-limit attribution, and shared-client availability with only test/CI proof currently visible.

options.title: Refresh and land this PR
options.body: Resolve current-main drift, add live proof for multi-client rate-limit isolation plus resume/turn routing, and use this PR as the single fix path.

options.title: Split into smaller PRs
options.body: Land rate-limit scoping, turn routing, and resume retirement separately if maintainers want lower blast radius and easier live proof per piece.

options.title: Pause until live proof exists
options.body: Keep the branch open but do not merge until a real Codex app-server run demonstrates the changed behavior with private details redacted.

recommendation.title: Refresh and land this PR
recommendation.body: Resolve current-main drift, add live proof for multi-client rate-limit isolation plus resume/turn routing, and use this PR as the single fix path.
